claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure containing multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A framework combining machine learning, reduced-order physics simulations, and microstructural descriptors can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness for HfNbTiVAl10.
The hybrid framework will improve predictive accuracy relative to existing methods.
The hybrid framework will improve computational efficiency relative to existing methods.
Phase distributions and local chemical-fluctuation metrics can be extracted from high-resolution imaging and simulation data and supplied to a tailored machine-learning model.
Reduced-order physics-based solvers can be integrated with the tailored machine-learning model.
Phase composition or phase heterogeneity affects alloy mechanical properties.
Descriptors of multilevel chemical fluctuations link the microstructural state of HfNbTiVAl10 to its macroscale mechanical properties.
Capturing chemical heterogeneity and hierarchical structure allows physics-informed machine learning to relate microstructural variations to deformation mechanisms.
Capturing chemical heterogeneity and hierarchical structure allows physics-informed machine learning to relate microstructural variations to fracture mechanisms.
Using reduced-order physics and microstructural descriptors reduces reliance on computationally expensive full-scale simulations.
The integrated framework will exceed 90% predictive accuracy against experiments for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The integrated framework will reduce computational time by roughly one order of magnitude relative to full CALPHAD or ab initio methods.
Phenomenological rules have approximately 72% predictive accuracy.
Phenomenological rules, CALPHAD, and machine learning have been used as alloy-search or prediction approaches.
Standalone CALPHAD, unguided machine learning, or ab initio calculations individually require excessive computational resources or have lower accuracy for yield strength and fracture toughness.
The model may become unreliable when phase segregation or chemical-fluctuation scales lie outside its training distribution.
The model may become unreliable at extreme strain rates or temperatures where deformation mechanisms change substantially.
Prior evidence supports combining machine learning with physics-based models to improve prediction accuracy and efficiency.
